The chart shows four subplots labeled (a), (b), (c), and (d).
- In subplots **(a)**, **(b)**, and **(d)**, the points are separated primarily along the vertical axis (y-axis, labeled $v$). There is a horizontal dashed line around $v=10^{-3}$ that acts as a boundary. In (a) and (d), green points are above and blue points are below. In (b), blue points are above and green points are below. Despite the color swap in (b), the *direction* of the split is horizontal.
- In subplot **(c)**, the points are separated primarily along the horizontal axis (x-axis, labeled $S$). The blue points are clustered on the left (low $S$) and the green points are clustered on the right (high $S$). This is a vertical split.

Therefore, subplot (c) has a different split direction compared to the others.

(c)
